findings.title: Billing's tax/total math smuggled into shared/lib as "generic money math"
findings.what_a_dev_would_write: A tired dev adding to the invoice table sees formatMoney already lives in shared/lib/format.ts and thinks "money math belongs together and is reusable." They create apps/web/src/shared/lib/money.ts exporting netMinor/taxMinor/grossMinor over a generic RatedLine {quantity, unitPriceMinor, taxRateBps} — an exact copy of billing's core rule (quantity*unitPrice + half-up Decimal tax on basis points) — and rewire InvoiceLinesTable.vue to call the shared helpers instead of billing/core/rules.ts.
findings.why_violates_spirit: The line-total-with-tax formula is billing DOMAIN CORE — README worked example 1 explicitly places tax/total math in slices/billing/core/rules.ts ("Delete Vue and it still makes sense? Yes — a discount changes line/total math -> billing/core"). shared/ is supposed to hold ZERO domain knowledge (rule 7). Now the global primitive layer encodes billing's tax model (bps rate, half-up rounding, minor-units line shape). A second slice would not tax lines this way; the concept is not "genuinely the same everywhere," it just looks like arithmetic. The machine only greps shared/ for domain NOUNS in filenames/exported-symbol names, so netMinor/taxMinor/grossMinor/RatedLine — all noun-free — sail through while carrying pure billing rules.
findings.which_rule_should_have_caught_it: Constitution rule 7 (shared/ holds zero domain knowledge) and rule 4/6 (domain rules live in core). The 'No domain noun under shared/' structure test is the intended guard but only inspects filenames and export-declaration identifiers, never the body of a function — so domain logic under a noun-free name is invisible to it. depcruise happily allows the ui->shared/lib edge.

findings.title: A shared StatusPill that hard-codes both slices' status semantics (one costume, two reasons to change)
findings.what_a_dev_would_write: Noticing billing's InvoiceStatusBadge and scheduling's AppointmentCard both keep a status->badge-variant Record, a dev DRYs them into shared/ui/status-pill/StatusPill.vue with a `status: string` prop and one VARIANT_BY_STATUS map containing BOTH billing statuses (draft/issued/paid/void) and scheduling statuses (scheduled/completed/cancelled), then makes both slice components delegate to it.
findings.why_violates_spirit: This is rule 6's "two components wearing one costume": the shared component changes for two unrelated reasons (billing invoice lifecycle vs scheduling appointment lifecycle) and now knows the color semantics of two different domains — domain knowledge in a global primitive (rule 7). It is used in exactly 2 places for DIFFERENT reasons, so rule 7 says duplicate, don't promote ("Two usages: leave it duplicated"). Yet nothing bites: the status values ("scheduled", "cancelled", ...) live only as object-literal keys and template text, which the shared-domain-noun grep never inspects; the prop is a bare `status: string`, so no slice type crosses into shared and no domain noun appears in a filename or exported symbol.
findings.which_rule_should_have_caught_it: Constitution rule 6 (concern = reason to change; split components that change for two reasons) and rule 7 (deliberate promotion, no domain knowledge in shared/). The 'shared/ is domain-free' structure test is the nominal guard but only scans filenames + export declarations; domain status vocabularies embedded as string-literal map keys and a `status: string` prop are structurally invisible to it, and depcruise treats it as an ordinary slice->shared/ui edge.

findings.title: core/ reads the wall clock through a shared/lib seam, breaking rule purity/determinism
findings.what_a_dev_would_write: To avoid threading `today` from the composition root onto the invoice detail page, a dev adds shared/lib/clock.ts (`now() => new Date()`) and a convenience billing/core/policy.ts helper `isOverdueNow(invoice)` that calls `isOverdue(invoice, now())`, then surfaces it as an `overdue` computed in useInvoiceDetail and passes it to the status badge.
findings.why_violates_spirit: core/ is supposed to be pure and deterministic: both core files carry the explicit invariant "today/now is always passed IN ... a clock is never read here," and rule 4 says every core/ folder's tests must still pass if you deleted Vue. isOverdueNow makes billing/core non-deterministic — its result depends on when it runs, so a core-level test of it is inherently time-dependent. The clock read is laundered through shared/lib, which is a legal core->shared/lib edge, and `now()` is a plain global Date() (no vue, no fetch, no restricted npm), so the framework-free / no-restricted-imports guards see nothing wrong. Impurity, not a framework import, is the smell, and no check measures purity.
findings.which_rule_should_have_caught_it: Constitution rule 4 (core is framework-free AND, by the documented invariant, clock-free/deterministic). The enforcement suite only encodes 'framework-free' as an npm allow-list + no-restricted-imports on vue/pinia/fetch; it has no notion of side effects or clock access, and core->shared/lib is an explicitly allowed edge, so a Date() read reached indirectly through shared/lib passes every gate.

notes: Baseline verified green before starting (86 modules; 28 tests; verify PASS). Each finding built, checked with all 5 commands, and confirmed green in isolation with `git checkout . && git clean -fd` between them. Final applied state = all three combined (they are additive/independent): re-verified green — vp lint exit 0, vue-tsc clean, depcruise 'no dependency violations found (90 modules, 234 dependencies)', vitest 28/28 passed, verify:enforcement 'PASS: all 13 rules bit'. Files left applied in /home/wds/vise-mb2: new shared/lib/money.ts, shared/lib/clock.ts, shared/ui/status-pill/*; modified billing/core/policy.ts, billing/ui/{components/InvoiceLinesTable.vue,components/InvoiceStatusBadge.vue,composables/useInvoiceDetail.ts,views/InvoiceDetailView.vue}, scheduling/ui/components/AppointmentCard.vue. Common thread: the machine enforces STRUCTURE (file location, import direction, framework/npm allow-lists, domain nouns in shared filenames/exported symbol names) but cannot see SEMANTICS — domain logic under noun-free names, domain vocabularies as string literals/props, or impurity reached via a legal shared/lib edge all slip through.
